analysis: Aminoglycosides are known to cause ototoxicity, primarily affecting the cochlear hair cells. The damage is more pronounced in the outer hair cells, particularly in the basal area of the cochlea. This is because the basal area is responsible for high-frequency sound detection, and aminoglycosides tend to affect these frequencies first. The consensus in medical literature supports that the outer hair cells in the basal area are most susceptible to damage from aminoglycosides.
